name: Citizenship by Registration

requirement_groups.name: Person of Indian origin, ordinarily resident in India

requirements.blocker_text: Person of Indian origin ordinarily resident in India for 7 years immediately before applying.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 7 years' ordinary residence in India.

requirements.blocker_text: Married to a citizen of India and ordinarily resident in India for 7 years immediately before applying. The provision is gender-neutral on its face -- 'a person married to a citizen of India' -- unlike several comparable marriage-based citizenship routes elsewhere in this dataset.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 7 years' ordinary residence in India while the marriage subsists.

evidence_required.document: Proof of Indian origin or registered marriage certificate
Proof of ordinary residence in India (7 years)

sources.title: Karma Law (law firm legal analysis) -- The Citizenship Act, 1955: Section 5 registration categories include persons of Indian origin ordinarily resident in India for 7 years, and persons married to a citizen of India and ordinarily resident in India for 7 years, among other categories (minor children of citizens, Commonwealth-country citizens, former citizens)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (India). STATUS: DRAFT -- India's own official legislative repository (indiacode.nic.in) could not be fetched directly in this build (returned an error page), so this file relies on secondary legal-analysis sources (tier 3, law-firm-published). FIGURE CONFLICT, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: two independent tier-3 sources (this one, and a separate CaseMine legal database entry) state the residence period as 7 years for both the Indian-origin and marriage categories; however, Refworld's UNHCR-hosted (tier 2) summary of the same Section 5 stated the period as 5 years for both categories. This dataset models the 7-year figure since it is corroborated by two independent secondary sources against Refworld's one, but this is disclosed as an open conflict rather than a settled fact -- a user relying on this figure should verify directly with an Indian mission or the Ministry of Home Affairs before treating either number as final. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING: the marriage-based registration provision is gender-neutral on its face ('a person married to a citizen of India'), unlike the many one-directional gendered marriage-citizenship provisions found elsewhere in this dataset (Qatar, Bahrain, Nigeria, Sudan, Pakistan, Somalia) -- consistent with India's gender-neutral descent provision (see in_citizenship_by_descent.json). dual_citizenship_allowed FALSE per India's constitutional prohibition.
